newsitem.title: FRANCE: Matif says signed CME deal on contracts trade.
newsitem.headline: Matif says signed CME deal on contracts trade.

text.p: French futures and options exchange MATIF said on Wednesday it had signed an agreement with the Chicago Mercantile Exchange to allow trade in MATIF's interest rate contracts on the U.S. exchange.
A MATIF spokeswoman said the agreement would begin with trade in the French bond future and options on the contract.
She said that after 1530 GMT, the close of the MATIF open outcry session, the bond contracts will be traded both on GLOBEX and on the CME trading floor.
From 1700 GMT, the bond contracts will be traded only on the Chicago exchange, until the end of its open outcry session.
MATIF said in a statement the agreement was initially for a period of five years.

While the 10-year French franc bond future and options contracts will be the first to trade, the statement said the agreement applied to MATIF interest products with "a maturity of more than one year, denominated in francs, Ecu, the euro, or any other European currency."

MATIF said in the statement the agreement was part of its strategy for adapting to the move to a single European currency as it would allow increased availability of euro-denominated contracts using open outcry, a proven, liquid means of trading.
It said in the statement the recent modification of the notional terms of its underlying bond had been the first step as it paved the way for the introduction of a medium-term bond futures contract.

Gerard Pfauwadel, MATIF president, said "We are very satisfied with this agreement which constitutes an important milestone in our committed strategy of preparation for monetary union and confirms the view of MATIF as the market leader in euro products."

Jack Sandner, president of CME, said "We are proud to reinforce our partnership with MATIF, which, bearing in mind its expertise in long-term interest products ... and thanks to the driving role of France in the prepartion of monetary union, will be among the market leaders for euro contracts."
